clock: HPD correction windows run from service of an HPD Notice of Violation, not from a tenant's photo or letter. HPD considers a mailed notice served five days after mailing; heat and hot water notices are served at inspection.

classTable.label: Immediately hazardous — lead-based paint, window guards, mold, mice/cockroaches, rats
Immediately hazardous — heat and hot water

facts.prompt: Is water actively dripping or flowing right now?
facts.help: A stain or damp patch with no water coming through counts as "no".

options.label: No, it's a stain or damage

variants.quote: All other class C (e.g. … active leaks …) — 24 hours
variants.plainEnglish: The owner must keep the building and its plumbing in good repair. HPD lists active leaks among its 24-hour Class C examples.
variants.note: HPD's inspector assigns the class. About 11% of leak violations issued since 2025 were Class C.

variants.quote: Class B Hazardous — 30 Days from date of service
variants.plainEnglish: The owner must keep the building and its plumbing in good repair, which includes finding the source of the water and fixing the damage.
variants.note: HPD's inspector assigns the class. About 80% of leak violations issued since 2025 were Class B.

facts.prompt: About how much visible mold is in this room?
facts.help: A standard door is about 20 sq ft. Mold only on tile or grout isn't covered by this rule.

options.label: Less than 10 sq ft (smaller than half a door)
30 sq ft or more (a big patch of wall)

variants.quote: less than ten square feet in a room … non-hazardous
variants.plainEnglish: Under 10 sq ft of mold in one room is a Class A violation. The owner must also fix the cause, like a leak.
variants.note: An uncorrected Class A mold violation can be upgraded to Class B.

variants.quote: between ten square feet and thirty square feet … hazardous
variants.plainEnglish: 10 to 29 sq ft of mold in one room is a Class B violation. The owner must also fix the cause, like a leak.
variants.note: An uncorrected Class B mold violation can be upgraded to Class C.

variants.quote: greater than or equal to thirty square feet in a room … immediately hazardous
variants.plainEnglish: 30 sq ft or more of mold in one room is a Class C violation with a 21-day window. The owner must also fix the cause.
variants.note: HPD can postpone a Class C mold deadline by up to 14 days.

variants.quote: Class C Heat and Hot Water — No time
variants.plainEnglish: Hot water must be at least 120°F, 365 days a year. HPD gives no time to correct it, so the notice asks for repair within 24 hours.

variants.citation: NYC Admin. Code §27-2029(a) (as amended by Local Law 86 of 2017)
variants.quote: Class C Heat and Hot Water — No time
variants.plainEnglish: Oct 1 to May 31: at least 68°F from 6 AM to 10 PM when it's below 55°F outside, and at least 62°F overnight. HPD gives no time to correct it, so the notice asks for repair within 24 hours.

variants.reason: Heat is only required from October 1 to May 31, so there's no heat violation outside heat season. Hot water is required all year.

variants.quote: the presence of cockroaches, mice or rats … shall constitute an immediately hazardous violation
variants.plainEnglish: Mice, cockroaches or rats in an apartment or common area are a Class C violation with a 21-day window. The owner must also seal the ways they get in.
variants.note: HPD can postpone a Class C pest deadline by up to 14 days.

variants.quote: pests other than cockroaches, mice, or rats … shall be a hazardous violation
variants.plainEnglish: Pests other than mice, cockroaches or rats, such as bedbugs, are a Class B violation.

options.label: My apartment door can't be locked
My apartment door locks, but the lock is damaged
The building's entrance door won't lock
A door that should close by itself doesn't

variants.quote: All other class C (e.g. … defective door locks …) — 24 hours
variants.plainEnglish: The owner must provide a working key lock on every apartment's entrance door — in most apartment buildings, a heavy-duty latch and dead bolt.
variants.note: HPD's inspector assigns the class; HPD lists defective door locks among its 24-hour Class C examples.

variants.quote: Class B Hazardous — 30 Days from date of service
variants.plainEnglish: The owner must keep the apartment entrance lock in good repair.
variants.note: HPD's inspector assigns the class. Apartment door-lock repair violations since 2025 were mostly Class B.

variants.quote: All other class C (e.g. … defective door locks …) — 24 hours
variants.plainEnglish: The owner must keep the building's entrance door and its lock in good repair.
variants.note: HPD's inspector assigns the class. Building-entrance lock violations since 2025 were mostly Class C.

variants.quote: Class C Self-Closing Doors — 14 Days from date of service
variants.plainEnglish: Apartment entrance and stairwell doors must close and latch by themselves, to slow a fire.

facts.help: Habitable fills this in from the city's building records when it can.

facts.prompt: Does a child under 6 live here, or spend 10+ hours a week here?
facts.help: In older buildings this makes peeling paint a presumed lead hazard. Habitable remembers your answer for this case.

facts.prompt: Is the plaster underneath cracked or broken too?

variants.quote: These violations are all Class "C" immediately hazardous violations
variants.plainEnglish: In a building built before 1960 where a child under 6 lives, peeling paint is presumed to be lead paint. It's a Class C violation and must be fixed with lead-safe work practices.
variants.note: Lead paint is especially dangerous for young children. NYC Health: call 311 for free inspection help.

variants.quote: Class B Hazardous — 30 Days from date of service
variants.plainEnglish: Broken or defective plaster with peeling paint is usually written as a Class B violation.
variants.note: HPD's inspector assigns the class. "Broken or defective plastered surfaces and paint" violations are mostly Class B.

variants.quote: Class A Non-Hazardous — 90 Days from date of service
variants.plainEnglish: Ordinary peeling paint is a Class A violation. Owners must also repaint apartments every three years.
variants.note: In NYC data, every ordinary peeling-paint violation (§27-2013) since 2025 was Class A.

notCovered.reason: This doesn't look like one of the six conditions Habitable covers. You can still pick one yourself, or log it as a general note with no class.
